questions.question: Which among the following instruments is used to measure the humidity of the air or a gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**Hygrometer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A hygrometer is an instrument used to measure the amount of water vapor or humidity in the air or gas.
 
 
• There are different types of hygrometers, such as mechanical, electrical, and digital, that use different principles to measure humidity.
 
• **A hygrometer is an instrument used to measure relative humidity**.
 
 
• A** psychrometer **is an example of a hygrometer.
 
• A **psychrometer uses two thermometers to measure relative humidity,** one measures the dry-bulb temperature, and the other measures the wet-bulb temperature.
 
 
 
• **Humidity is the measure of the amount of moisture in the air.**
 
 
 
• **Anemometer,** on the other hand, is an instrument used to measure **wind speed and direction.**
 
• ** A bolometer** is an instrument used to measure** electromagnetic radiation, such as infrared or microwave radiation.**
 
• ** A hydrometer **is an instrument used to measure the** density or specific gravity of liquids**.
 
 
• Hydrometer operates based on the Archimedes principle that a solid body displaces its own weight within a liquid in which it floats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **INSTRUMENT**
 **MEASUREMENT**
 
 

 Hydrometer
 Specific gravity or density of a liquid.
 
 

 Pyrometer
 Temperature.
 
 

 Lactometer
 Amount of water in the milk or purity of milk.

questions.question: Only Indian citizens above the age of ________ years are eligible for the appointment of the Governor of a State.
questions.solution:

• The key word in the question is "Governor of a State", which refers to the constitutional head of a state in India.

**Governor:**

 
• Under **Article 155 of the Indian Constitution,** the Governor of a State **shall be appointed by the President.**
 
• A person should have completed 35 years of age to be appointed as Governor.
 
• The Governor shall hold office at the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years and the State election commissioner for elections to the Panchayats. 
 
• By the** 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956,** the s**ame person can be appointed as a governor for two or more states.**
 
• **He is entitled to receive such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as may be determined by Parliament.**
 
• **When he is appointed for two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable to him are shared by the respective states in such proportion as determined by the President. **
 
• A governor whose term has expired may be reappointed in the same state or any other state.

questions.question: ________ was passed in 2019 and as a result of which the security of Prime Minister of India and other former Prime Ministers was restricted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SPECIAL PROTECTION GROUP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2019.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• This act was passed by the Indian parliament in 2019 to amend the Special Protection Group (SPG) Act of 1988.
 
• As a result of this amendment, the SPG security cover was restricted to only the serving Prime Minister of India and his/her immediate family members residing with him/her at the official residence.
 
• The security cover for former **Prime Ministers was downgraded to Z⁺ category security cover provided by the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**.
 
• The aim of this amendment was to rationalize and optimize the deployment of SPG personnel and resources.

**The SPG**

 
• It was raised in** 1985 to provide proximate security cover to the Prime Minister, former Prime Ministers, and their immediate family members.** Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• It was created after the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• Parliament passed the **SPG Act (1988) **dedicating the group to protecting the Prime Ministers of India.
 
• After** Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination (1991), the SPG Act was amended**, offering SPG protection to all former Prime Ministers and their families for a **period of at least 10 years.**

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of ‘untouchability’ and prohibits its practice in any shape or form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 17.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article **17 of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of ‘untouchability’ **and prohibits its practice in any shape or form.
 
• In fact, the enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law.
 
• In fact, this is **one of the few fundamental rights which is available to individuals.**
 
• To make the untouchability **law further strong, parliament passed an Untouchability (offenses) Act in 1955.**
 
• However, this act was further **amended and also renamed in the year 1976 as the Protection of the Civil Rights Act, of 1955.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Article 14 - Equality before law.**

 
• The said Article is in two parts – while it commands the State not to deny to any person **‘equality before the law’,**
 
• It also commands the State not to deny the ‘equal protection of the laws’.
 
• Equality before the law prohibits discrimination. It is a negative concept.
 
• The concept of ‘equal protection of the laws’ requires the State to give special treatment to persons in different situations in order to establish equality amongst all. It is positive in character. Therefore, the necessary corollary to this would be that equals would be treated equally, whilst un-equals would have to be treated unequally

**Article 15- Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.**

 
• It secures the citizens from every sort of discrimination by the State, on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth or any of them. However, this Article does not prevent the State from making any special provisions for women or children.
 
• It also allows the State to extend special provisions for socially and economically backward classes for their advancement. It applies to the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) as well.

**Article 16- Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. **

 
• It assures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prevents the State from any sort of discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, or any of them.
 
• This Article also provides the autonomy to the State to grant special provisions for the backward classes, under-represented States, SC & ST for posts under the State.
 
• Local candidates may also be given preference in certain posts. Reservation of posts for people of a certain religion or denomination in a religious or denominational institution will not be deemed illegal. 

**Article 17 - Abolition of Untouchability**

 
• The practice of untouchability is an offense and anyone doing so is punishable by law.
 
• The Untouchability Offences Act of 1955 (renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act in 1976) provided penalties for preventing a person from entering a place of worship or from taking water from a tank or well.

questions.question: At independence, about 75 percent of India's population was dependent on _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** agricultural.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of India's independence in **1947, approximately 75 percent of the country's population relied on agriculture for their livelihoods.**
 
• Agriculture played a central role in the rural economy, with a majority of the rural population engaged in farming or related agricultural activities.
 
• Most agricultural practices in India were characterized by **subsistence farming,** where farmers grew crops primarily to meet the needs of their own families and local communities.
 
• Agricultural practices were predominantly labor-intensive, with limited use of modern machinery or technology in farming operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural population distribution according to Census 2011:**
 
• According to the **2011 census, the majority of India's agricultural population resided in rural areas**, reflecting the strong rural-urban divide in agricultural distribution.
 
• The census data revealed that a **significant portion of India's population, approximately 67 percent, **was engaged in agricultural activities, highlighting the continued importance of agriculture in the country's economy.
 
• The census also highlighted regional disparities in agricultural population distribution, with certain states and regions having a higher concentration of agricultural workers compared to others.
 
• The census data indicated a trend of fragmented landholdings in India, with a large number of farmers cultivating small plots of land.
 
• **This pattern of small-scale farming has implications for productivity and agricultural practices.**
 
• The census revealed a gender disparity in the agricultural workforce, with a majority of agricultural workers being male.
 
• However, it also indicated a significant** contribution by women to agricultural activities, highlighting their crucial role in the sector.**

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the “Lal-Bal-Pal” of the freedom movement of India?

The correct answer is__** Lala Lajpat Rai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai of Punjab, Bal Gangadhar Tilak of Maharashtra, and Bipin Chandra Pal of Bengal were popularly known as Lal Bal Pal**.
 
• They advocated the Swadeshi movement involving the boycott of all imported items and the use of Indian-made goods in 1907 during the anti-Partition **agitation in Bengal which began in 1905.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Lala Lajpat Rai**

 
 
• ​Born in undivided **Punjab on 28 January 1865.**
 
• In 1895, he started the Punjab National Bank—the first Indian bank to begin solely with the Indian capital.
 
• He focused his efforts on a self-sufficient India.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**
 
 
• Tilak was a loud voice against the British rule.
 
• His articles in newspapers like Kesari, which he founded in 1881 had earned him strong support from like-minded people like the Chapekar brothers.
 
• **With the slogan “Swarajya majha janmasiddha hakka ahe… Ani to me milavnarach,**” he ignited strong patriotism among his Marathi peers. “Swarajya (self-rule) is my birthright, and I shall have it” became a popular chant during the freedom struggle.
 
• Tilak was the “Father of the Indian Unrest.” according to Britishers.
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal** ​
 
 
• The father of revolutionary thoughts, Bipin Chandra Pal, was born to a wealthy family in Sylhet, Bengal Presidency (now in Bangladesh).
 
• Pal was a journalist by profession and had always turned to his pen to unite efforts of Indians for Swarajya and Swadeshi goods.

questions.question: The species that _______ a bare area are called pioneer species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**invade.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pioneer species are the first organisms to colonize a newly formed or disturbed area.**
 
• These species are able to survive in **harsh conditions and are usually fast-growing and hardy.**
 
• The sequential, gradual, and predictable changes in the species composition in an area are called succession or ecological succession.
 
• The **entire sequence of communities that successively changes in a given area is called sere(s).**
 
• The individual transitional communities are termed seral stages or seral communities.
 
• The community that is in near equilibrium with the environment is called a climax community.
 
• The species that invade a bare area are called pioneer species.​

**Explanation:**

 
• **Lichens are the pioneer species on a bare area or Xerarch condition.**
 
• The lichen secretes some acids to dissolve rock and help in weathering and soil formation.
 
• Later, some small bryophytes invade and hold a small amount of soil.
 
• The **bryophytes are succeded by herbs, shrubs, and ultimately big trees.**
 
• At last, a stable climax forest is formed.
 
• The xerophytic habitat gets converted into a mesophytic one.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Hydrach succession** takes place in wet areas or water, leading to successional series progress from hydric to mesic conditions.
 
• **The pioneer species are phytoplankton.**

questions.question: What is the rank of India in terms of Human Development Index 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**132.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• India is ranked 132 out of 191 in the Human Development Index, 2021.
 
• According to a report released by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), with an HDI value of 0.633, India is ranked 132 out of 191 countries in the 2021 Human Development Index.
 
• India has been placed in the medium human development category.
 
• In the 2020 report, India was 0.645 and ranked 131st among 189 countries.
 
• Sri Lanka has got 73rd rank in the Human Development Index. With this, China has been ranked 79th, Bhutan 127th, Bangladesh 129th, Nepal 143rd and Pakistan 161st.
 
• Switzerland has been ranked first in the report of the United Nations Human Development Index.
 
 
• This is followed by Norway, then Iceland, Hong Kong, and Australia in fifth place.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Human development is a measure of a nation's health, education, and average income.
 
• It has declined for two consecutive years - 2020 and 2021 - reversing five years of progress.
 
• What is the concept of human development:-
 
 
• Human development refers to the expansion of all those economic, social, cultural and political areas which are necessary for the development of human beings.
 
• Knowledge, better standard of living, equality and social justice, human security and human rights, environmental sustainability, participation in social and political life, health and longevity, etc. are all included in the characteristics of human development, thus human development is an important end of economic prosperity.
